title: Event payload transport does not establish validated audit history
question: Compare exact producer payload preservation with required Audit Event fields, actor validity and duplicate-event rejection at the actual recording boundary.

evidence.title: Outbox recording preserves payload but does not validate Audit Event meaning
explanation: OutboxEventAdapter serializes the supplied producer payload with ObjectMapper, creates a pending OutboxEventEntity and saves it. The payload is separate from the generated transport UUID and creation time; transporting an Audit-shaped JSON object does not itself validate its financial event fields.

At this isolated recording boundary, a valid complete event and an event with unknown actor omitted survive the payload round trip. The method has no Audit-specific timestamp or actor validation and does not look up an existing producer eventId before save. Its technical row UUID is not a uniqueness check on payload event identity.

On 2026-11-23, the unchanged pinned adapter/entity/repository interface were compiled and invoked with JDK 21.0.12.1, Jackson 2.19.1, Spring 6.2.8 and Spring Data JPA 3.5.1. A repository port double stored the actual entities emitted by record without adding validation; observations decoded getPayload rather than copying expected results. No SQL, transaction rollback, relay, actor authorization or deployment-level audit policy was executed. Required control may exist outside this function; the result is not a general defect or a full Audit implementation claim.

historical_publications.title: java-payment-core — Outbox payload transport and Audit applicability
explanation: A bounded native outbox probe retained producer fields through serialization and a repository port double. This provides transport context for Audit attribution; it did not evaluate committed Audit Event validity, identity uniqueness or append history. No comparable Audit conformance score is published.

Audit-shaped JSON is observed inside the native transport payload. Generated outbox IDs/times are technical metadata and are not substituted for producer event identity/occurrence time. Repository storage was a port double; persistence, SQL constraints, transaction atomicity and controls in other layers are outside this evaluation.
